fixes.title: Sequence recovery checkpoint is stored at a hardcoded shared path, so a brand-new profile was offered another database's interrupted run -- and discarding it deleted that run's recovery data
fixes.summary: The desktop shell now derives the checkpoint directory from the OPEN DATABASE (`resolveDefaultDatabaseFile().parent/checkpoints`) instead of `getApplicationSupportDirectory()`. Every Skotiq GUI on a machine shares one support folder, so the old anchor let instance B -- pointed at its own database via SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR -- find, be offered, and (via the modal's only dismissal, Discard) DELETE instance A's checkpoint plus its .bak. Anchoring on the database directory makes a checkpoint that does not belong to the open database structurally unreachable. A guarded one-time adoption carries a checkpoint written by an older build forward from the legacy location, but only when SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR is unset -- in that layout there is exactly one database on the machine and SingleInstanceLock guarantees no other process is running against it, so the legacy file provably belongs to this database. With the override set the legacy file is left alone rather than re-creating the defect. Also reordered set-dir before adopt so a slow/failing adoption cannot leave tonight's run with no checkpoint directory at all.
fixes.not_done: The reporter's proposal to stamp the owning database id INTO the checkpoint and refuse a mismatch needs a native + CheckpointInfo change (see needs_shared_change). The path anchor closes the reported harm without it. The reporter's third sub-claim (dialog offers a run whose executor_state is Completed) is REFUTED and was not 'fixed': CheckpointInfo.canResume already requires is_active && state in {Running,Paused} (checkpoint.rs can_resume) and app_shell returns noRecovery when !canResume -- the verifier reproduced executor_state=Paused live and identified the reporter's evidence as a later snapshot written by mark_completed().
fixes.wiring_severed: The first test pumps the REAL AppShell with a recording SequencerBackend and separate mocked documents/support folders, and asserts on the path the shell actually hands to sequencerSetCheckpointDir. Nothing calls the new helper directly.
revert_check: app_shell.dart:_performCheckpointCheck -- replaced `final checkpointDir = await resolveGuiCheckpointDirectory();` with `final checkpointDir = await getApplicationSupportDirectory();` => FAIL: Expected '/tmp/ns-checkpoint-EVBBQF/documents/Skotiq/checkpoints' Actual '/tmp/ns-checkpoint-EVBBQF/support'. Restored -> pass.

app_shell.dart:adoptLegacyGuiCheckpoint -- deleted the three lines `final override = env[skotiqDatabaseDirEnv]?.trim(); if (override != null && override.isNotEmpty) return;` => FAIL: 'a database-directory override leaves the shared file alone' Expected: false Actual: <true>. Restored -> pass.
fixes.needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/checkpoint.rs + packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/backend/sequencer_status.dart (CheckpointInfo): persist an owning database/profile identifier in the checkpoint payload, expose it on CheckpointInfo, and have app_shell refuse recovery on a mismatch. That is defence in depth against a future path collision; it is not required for the reported repro. Separately, apps/desktop/lib/headless/host_checkpoint_directory.dart still anchors the HEADLESS host on <appSupport>/checkpoints; it should move to the same database-derived root for the same reason.

fixes.title: Equipment readiness panel omits the mount entirely when it is disconnected
fixes.summary: Confirmed real and diagnosed, but every line that has to change is outside my ownership list. The readiness report is built in skotiq_core, not on the equipment screen: readiness_provider.dart:104-112 filters camera AND mount out of offlineProfileDevices ('already covered by the critical-devices item'), while readiness_models.dart _buildCriticalDevices returns exactly ONE item for the highest-priority fault -- so the `if (!cameraConnected)` branch returns first and the `if (!mountConnected)` branch below it is unreachable whenever both are down. Result: with all four profile devices offline the panel names Camera, Focuser and Filter Wheel and never mentions the mount. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/widgets/equipment_readiness_panel.dart (which I do own) only renders ReadinessReport; adding a mount row there would duplicate the model's authority and is exactly the 'relocate the defect' move, so I did not.
fixes.test: none written -- the fix is in a package I do not own

fixes.title: Red night theme renders full-saturation blue, cyan and green accent swatches
fixes.summary: Confirmed, located precisely, and found to be WORSE than reported -- but the file is outside my ownership list. The swatch row is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/settings_widgets/settings_color_and_path_inputs.dart (`SettingsColorPicker.accentColors` at :75-83 and `_buildColorCircle` at :109), mounted from screens/settings/widgets/appearance_settings.dart:70-87. The hex list is exactly the pixels the reporter sampled (#5B9EC4, #10B981, #F59E0B, #EF4444, #2878A8, #EC4899, #06B6D4) and `_buildColorCircle` paints them raw, with no reference to `colors.isRedNight`. The additional defect: `resolveSkotiqThemeData` (skotiq_ui/lib/src/theme/skotiq_theme.dart:43-44) returns the fixed `SkotiqTheme.redNight` for 'redNight' and never calls darkWithAccent/lightWithAccent, so in red night the accent selection has NO effect on anything. The control is therefore both a short-wavelength light source and inert -- it shows a live-looking selection that changes nothing.
fixes.test: none written -- the fix is in a package directory I do not own
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/appearance_settings.dart: because red night ignores the accent entirely, the honest fix is the reporter's second option -- do not render the picker at all in red night. In the 'Accent color' SettingRow replace `trailing: SettingsColorPicker(...)` with `trailing: settings.theme == 'redNight' ? const SettingsInlineNote('Red night uses a fixed red-only palette; accent colour applies to Dark and Light.') : SettingsColorPicker(...)` (or the existing disabled-row convention in settings_widgets.dart), and mirror the note in the row subtitle. That removes the cyan/green/blue pixels AND stops the app offering a choice it will not honour. If a swatch row is wanted in red night instead, `_buildColorCircle` already receives `SkotiqColors colors`, so gate on `colors.isRedNight` and paint Color.fromARGB(255, redChannelLuminance, 0, 0) with a Tooltip carrying the option's name (accentColors already stores it). Test to add: pump AppearanceSettings with theme 'redNight' and assert find.byType(SettingsColorPicker) findsNothing; and with 'dark' assert findsOneWidget.

fixes.title: Window minimize / maximize / close disappear below ~800px window width, leaving no way to close the app
fixes.summary: The compact bar the shell substitutes below ShellChromeMetrics.shellLayoutBreakpoint (`_MobileSettingsBar` in app_shell.dart) now renders the same caption buttons and the same drag-to-move region as the full TitleBar whenever the process owns a desktop window. Window controls are a property of the platform, not of the layout: the desktop runners set TitleBarStyle.hidden, so the OS draws no decorations at ANY width. Added `ShellChrome.isDesktopWindow` (kIsWeb-guarded, mirroring isNativeMobile) as the single predicate, promoted `_WindowControls` to public `WindowControls` and extracted the TitleBar's drag/double-tap GestureDetector into a public `WindowDragArea` so both layouts share one implementation rather than a copy. The wordmark became Flexible+ellipsis so a very narrow window truncates the title instead of overflowing or squeezing out the close button, and the trailing inset is dropped on desktop so the caption buttons sit flush to the window edge.
fixes.wiring_severed: Both tests pump the REAL AppShell at 760x700 and 1400x900 and search the rendered tree; the narrow case also asserts SkotiqBottomNavigation is present so the test is only meaningful while the compact layout is genuinely in play.
revert_check: app_shell.dart:_MobileSettingsBar -- deleted the `if (isDesktopWindow) ...[ const SizedBox(width: SkotiqTokens.spaceSm), WindowControls(colors: colors) ]` block => FAIL: 'Found 0 widgets with type "WindowControls"' at 760x700. Restored -> pass.
fixes.caveats: Alt+F4 and the window-manager keyboard/menu path always still closed the window, so the original 'no way to close the app' overstates it; 'no mouse-reachable window control' is accurate. Notifications and account buttons are still absent from the compact bar -- deliberately, that is the mobile chrome's density decision and both destinations remain reachable; only the controls that have no other affordance were restored. Worth knowing: apps/desktop/lib/main.dart:154 sets minimumSize Size(1200,700), so a user dragging the frame cannot normally reach the breakpoint -- but window_manager's minimum is advisory and a tiling WM or xdotool (which is how the auditor hit it) forces the size anyway, so the compact layout has to be self-sufficient.

fixes.title: The 'Deleted <profile>' snackbar never auto-dismisses and covers the entire status bar
fixes.summary: Set `persist: false` (plus `showCloseIcon: true`) on the delete-undo SnackBar. The verifier's diagnosis is correct and the original proposed fix would have changed nothing: `duration: const Duration(seconds: 6)` was already there and was INERT, because Flutter 3.44's SnackBar constructor does `persist = persist ?? action != null` and ScaffoldMessengerState's timer callback returns without hiding when snackBar.persist is true. I confirmed both lines in the pinned SDK (snack_bar.dart:303, scaffold.dart:618-622) and that SnackBarThemeData has NO persist field -- so this cannot be fixed globally in the app theme and every action-carrying SnackBar has to opt out individually.
fixes.wiring_severed: The test drives the real EquipmentScreen: long-press the profile -> Delete -> confirm Delete, then asserts the bar is still up at 4 s and gone by 8 s with no interaction, and that the close icon inside the SnackBar dismisses it.
revert_check: equipment_screen.dart -- deleted the two lines `persist: false,` and `showCloseIcon: true,` => FAIL both tests: 'Found 1 widget with text "Undo"' after 8 s, and 'Found 0 widgets with icon IconData(U+0E16A)' for the close button. Restored -> pass.
fixes.needs_shared_change: SYSTEMIC -- the same one-line omission affects every other action-carrying SnackBar in the app, each of which currently never times out: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/session_recovery_checker.dart, widgets/quick_start_checker.dart, widgets/equipment_onboarding_launcher.dart, screens/settings/settings_screen.dart, screens/sequencer/widgets/session_report_dialog.dart, screens/sequencer/mobile_sequence_editor.dart, screens/analytics/widgets/science_analytics_tab/navigation_and_snapshots.dart. Each needs `persist: false` next to its existing duration. Worth also adding a lint/behavioural-audit rule for `action: SnackBarAction` without `persist:`, since the framework default silently re-introduces this on every new call site.

fixes.title: Diagnostic dump is described as 'recent log files' but bundles 7 days of logs from every Skotiq instance on the machine
fixes.summary: Fixed what this screen owns; the log scoping itself is in two packages I do not own. FIXED: (1) the save dialog no longer opens in the application bundle -- `resolveDumpSaveDirectory()` supplies an initialDirectory (Downloads, else Documents, both checked for existence) to chooseExportTarget, which previously forwarded null straight to file_selector.getSaveLocation so the picker started at the process working directory, i.e. a read-only install dir; (2) the screen scrolls, so the contents card can never clip the one button that produces a bug report; (3) the 'Recent log files' claim is gone. That third item is deliberately NOT presented as the fix -- I verified the export is worse than reported: LoggingService.exportLogs concatenates every file in the log dir with no time bound, and the native appender is `tracing_appender::rolling::daily` with NO max_log_files (bridge/src/lib.rs:337), so nothing is ever pruned and the dump grows without limit. Leaving a sentence the product knows to be false was the worse of the two options, so the card now says what the zip actually contains and warns before attaching it publicly.
fixes.not_done: The dump is still unbounded in time and still resolved from the shared application-support folder rather than the active data directory, so on a machine running more than one Skotiq it still carries other instances' capture paths and target names.
fixes.wiring_severed: The widget test pumps the real DiagnosticDumpScreen, taps 'Create dump' and captures the arguments that reach the file_selector platform channel's getSavePath (returning null so no real dump is written), so dropping the argument at the call site fails it.
revert_check: diagnostic_dump_screen.dart:_createDump -- deleted the line `initialDirectory: await resolveDumpSaveDirectory(),` => FAIL: 'Expected: not null Actual: <null> // null lets the picker open in the read-only app bundle'. Restored -> pass.
fixes.needs_shared_change: TWO changes, both required before the 'Recent log files' wording can honestly come back. (1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/logging_service.dart: exportLogs (:378-410) must accept a bound -- e.g. `Future<String> exportLogs(String outputPath, {Duration? maxAge})` -- and getLogFiles (:336-365) must filter on lastModified; DiagnosticDumpService._addLogsEntry should pass something like 48 h and record the actual span it exported in manifest.json. Separately the native appender at native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/lib.rs:337 should get `.max_log_files(n)` (RollingFileAppender builder) so the directory stops growing forever. (2) apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:61-68 resolves the log directory as getApplicationSupportDirectory()/logs, ignoring SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR even though it sets that variable four lines earlier; it should use the resolved data directory so two instances with different data dirs do not write into one log file. Until (2) lands, a dump from any instance contains every instance's logs.
